speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you've mentioned double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; can you tell me if your double vision worsens when you look up or to the side? Also, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that clarification; the fluctuating weakness with activity and improvement at rest is very telling. Have you experienced any muscle pain or cramping when these symptoms first started? REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Phosphokinase (CK)
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Cervical_Spine

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your CK levels are normal and you have no neck pain or sensory deficits, have you noticed any drooping eyelids or changes in the shape of your smile?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. Given the characteristic fluctuating weakness worsening with activity, ocular symptoms triggered by upward gaze, and the absence of CK elevation or sensory deficits, this presentation is classic for an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction. We should proceed with testing for acetylcholine receptor antibodies to confirm the diagnosis.
